tagline: Botanicals from the valley, nothing else.
sector: Craft botanical soda, better-for-you premium CPG
founded_place_size: Founded in the Hudson Valley, New York. Two founders working with a co-packer, three flavours, sold in upstate natural grocers and by direct-to-consumer subscription.
about: Fennhollow Botanical Soda makes three botanical sodas in the Hudson Valley: elderflower and lime, rhubarb and bitters, and spruce tip. Three dollars fifty a can, sold across upstate natural grocers and by subscription, produced through a co-packer whose cleared nutrition claim cannot be reworded. Two founders run everything and neither is a photographer. The whole brand lives on summer: sun lit, warm, natural, a little restrained. The spruce tip flavour steps to the front in August, so the summer campaign has to be built to be revisited as the season shifts.
audience: Twenty-five to forty, shopping the natural grocer aisle and reading the ingredient panel. Paying a premium for the promise that this is closer to a real thing than a mass soda.
price_positioning: Craft better-for-you at three fifty a can. Warmer and more human than a twelve-dollar apothecary tonic, and far more restrained and natural than a hyper-saturated ninety-nine-cent soda.

palette.name: Label Green
palette.usage: Every flavour name set on Warm Cream Ground or over a light part of a photograph, as fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf sets its flavour name and fennhollow_brand_note.pdf its title; the half point rule that splits every stacked flavour name; the co-packer's claim line may be Label Green, as on fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf. It is the only solid panel colour besides Warm Cream Ground.

palette.name: Warm Cream Ground
palette.usage: The main ground of every designed area, as on fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf and fennhollow_brand_note.pdf, and all type set on a Label Green panel.

palette.name: Afternoon Amber
palette.usage: A small price tag device with the price figure reversed out of it, as the price flag on fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf. Never a ground, panel, rule or type colour.

palette.name: Rhubarb Rose
palette.usage: Small letterspaced labels and the short thin rule set just above them, as the NOW POURING label and its rule on fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf. Never a ground, panel or body text.

palette.name: Deep Ink
palette.role: mandatory where body text sits on Warm Cream Ground
palette.usage: Body text, subheads, fine print and the sourcing line on Warm Cream Ground, as fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf sets its store name and sourcing line and fennhollow_brand_note.pdf its body. Never a ground or panel.

typography: Fennhollow Botanical Soda runs four steps. Step 01, Display and H1, is Staatliches Regular caps at 120 pt on 108 pt leading, tracked -5 thousandths, set as the poster flavour name stacked onto two centred lines split by a half point rule in Label Green. Step 02, Subheading and H2, is Staatliches Regular caps at 96 px on 104 px, tracked -5 thousandths, for the key visual headline, stepping down to 64 px on 70 px on a carousel page and still stacked on two centred lines. Step 03, Body, is Whitney Book at 30 px on 42 px, tracking 0, measure held to a maximum of 65 characters, with Whitney Semibold at the same size for subheads. Step 04, Fine print, is Whitney Book at 18 pt on 24 pt, tracked +15 thousandths, and it carries the co-packer's cleared claim line exactly as written. A flavour name is never set on a single line.
voice: Plain, warm, a little rural. Names the botanicals and the valley, not a lifestyle. The co-packer's cleared claim line stays exactly as written.
brand_assets_status: No written brand guidelines have ever existed and the founders asked for the first one to be created. Their brand note points to a printed swatch card that was never sent with the package, so the house green survives only as the printed label on the two studio can shots the brand owns. There is no lifestyle photography of any kind.
values: Real ingredients over additives, provable and legal image provenance the co-packer can be shown, and a cohesive look the next hire can build on rather than start from nothing.

type_system.signature_move: Every flavour name stacks onto two centred lines of Staatliches caps split by a half point rule in Label Green, so the stacked block registers before the words are read. Steps 01 and 02 both carry it.
rules: Never set a flavour name on a single line.
A flavour name always stacks onto two centred lines split by a half point rule in Label Green.
The co-packer's cleared claim line stays exactly as written and is never reworded.
Whitney Semibold is the subhead weight; body stays Whitney Book.
Do not fabricate a sellable product image for a missing flavour or packshot; a gap stays a declared gap.
Step 02 leading and step 04 tracking were supplied because the prose states none; every family in this scale is the brand's own.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds and panels are Warm Cream Ground or Label Green and nothing else; Warm Cream Ground is the main ground, as on fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf and fennhollow_brand_note.pdf. On Warm Cream Ground, flavour names and their half point rules are Label Green, and body text, subheads and fine print are Deep Ink; the co-packer's claim line may be Deep Ink or Label Green, as on fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf. A stacked flavour name never sits on a Label Green panel, where its rule would vanish. On a Label Green panel all type is Warm Cream Ground, as the can labels in fennhollow_packshot_01.jpg and fennhollow_packshot_02.jpg set pale type on the green. Type set directly over a photograph, which fennhollow_brand_note.pdf expects, is Deep Ink or Label Green over light areas and Warm Cream Ground over dark ones. Afternoon Amber is for a small price tag and Rhubarb Rose for small labels and thin rules; together they cover no more than 10% of the designed, non-photographic area and are never a ground, a panel or body text.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour or to type, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph: type sits directly on the photograph or on a solid block. The one tint is a thin Label Green rule above the fine print at 45% opacity, as fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf sets its foot rule, and nowhere else.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes (#3F6B3A, #F4ECD8, #E5AF54, #C56E68 and #2C2A24) for type, grounds, panels, rules, buttons or icons, with three exceptions carried from fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf: a price figure reversed out of an Afternoon Amber tag may be white, a town line under a store name may be the warm grey #57534A, and the one 45% Label Green rule above the fine print allowed under opacity reads as its tint. No neon or hyper-saturated colour and no glow anywhere in the design, which the brand places against a hyper-saturated ninety-nine-cent soda.
palette_rules.photography: Photographs keep their own corrected colour and are never recoloured toward the palette; the can's aluminium stays silver. The one exception is the printed can label: our green is the label green, and it must still read as our Label Green through every correction.
